passages.text: When Pashhur the priest, the son of Immer and the chief official in the house of the LORD, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things, he had Jeremiah the prophet beaten and put in the stocks at the Upper Gate of Benjamin, which was by the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Pashhur was a priest.
Pashhur was the son of Immer.
Pashhur was the chief official in the house of the LORD.
Jeremiah was a prophet.
Jeremiah prophesied these things.
Pashhur heard Jeremiah prophesy.
Pashhur beat Jeremiah the prophet.
Pashhur put Jeremiah in the stocks.
The stocks were at the Upper Gate of Benjamin.
The Upper Gate of Benjamin was by the house of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע פַּשְׁחוּר֙ בֶּן־ אִמֵּ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהֽוּא־ פָקִ֥יד נָגִ֖יד בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֶֽת־ יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ נִבָּ֖א אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃ וַיַּכֶּ֣ה פַשְׁח֔וּר אֵ֖ת יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹת֜וֹ עַל־ הַמַּהְפֶּ֗כֶת אֲשֶׁ֨ר בְּשַׁ֤עַר בִּנְיָמִן֙ הָֽעֶלְי֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: The next day, when Pashhur released Jeremiah from the stocks, Jeremiah said to him, “The LORD does not call you Pashhur, but Magor-missabib.
passages.sermon:
Pashhur was a priest and chief official in the house of the LORD.
He had put Jeremiah the prophet in the stocks.
The next day, Pashhur released Jeremiah from the stocks.
Jeremiah spoke to Pashhur.
Jeremiah said, “The LORD does not call you Pashhur.
The LORD calls you Magor-missabib.”
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיֹּצֵ֥א פַשְׁח֛וּר אֶֽת־ יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מִן־ הַמַּהְפָּ֑כֶת וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ לֹ֤א פַשְׁחוּר֙ קָרָ֤א יְהוָה֙ שְׁמֶ֔ךָ כִּ֖י אִם־ מָג֥וֹר מִסָּבִֽיב׃פ

passages.text: For this is what the LORD says: ‘I will make you a terror to yourself and to all your friends. They will fall by the sword of their enemies before your very eyes. And I will hand Judah over to the king of Babylon, and he will carry them away to Babylon and put them to the sword.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke these words.
The LORD said, “I will make you, Pashhur, a terror to yourself.
I will make you a terror to all your friends.
Your friends will fall by the sword of their enemies.
You will see this with your own eyes.
I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon.
The king of Babylon will take them away to Babylon.
He will strike them down with the sword.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֡ה הִנְנִי֩ נֹתֶנְךָ֨ לְמָג֜וֹר לְךָ֣ וּלְכָל־ אֹהֲבֶ֗יךָ וְנָֽפְל֛וּ בְּחֶ֥רֶב אֹיְבֵיהֶ֖ם וְעֵינֶ֣יךָ רֹא֑וֹת וְאֶת־ כָּל־ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֶתֵּן֙ בְּיַ֣ד מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֔ל וְהִגְלָ֥ם בָּבֶ֖לָה וְהִכָּ֥ם בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: I will give away all the wealth of this city—all its products and valuables, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah—to their enemies. They will plunder them, seize them, and carry them off to Babylon.
passages.sermon:
God spoke through Jeremiah.
God said he would give away all the wealth of this city.
God would give all the products of the city to its enemies.
God would give all the valuables of the city to its enemies.
God would give all the treasures of the kings of Judah to their enemies.
The enemies would plunder these things.
The enemies would seize these things.
The enemies would carry these things off to Babylon.
passages.original: וְנָתַתִּ֗י אֶת־ כָּל־ חֹ֙סֶן֙ הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את וְאֶת־ כָּל־ יְגִיעָ֖הּ וְאֶת־ כָּל־ יְקָרָ֑הּ וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ אוֹצְר֜וֹת מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה אֶתֵּן֙ בְּיַ֣ד אֹֽיְבֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְזָזוּם֙ וּלְקָח֔וּם וֶהֱבִיא֖וּם בָּבֶֽלָה׃

passages.text: And you, Pashhur, and all who live in your house, will go into captivity. You will go to Babylon, and there you will die and be buried—you and all your friends to whom you have prophesied these lies.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Pashhur was a leader in Jerusalem.
God spoke to Pashhur.
God said Pashhur and everyone living in his house would go into captivity.
They would be taken away as prisoners.
They would be brought to Babylon.
Pashhur would die in Babylon.
Pashhur would be buried in Babylon.
All of Pashhur’s friends would also die and be buried in Babylon.
Pashhur had prophesied lies to his friends.
His friends would share his fate.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֣ה פַשְׁח֗וּר וְכֹל֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בֵיתֶ֔ךָ תֵּלְכ֖וּ בַּשֶּׁ֑בִי וּבָבֶ֣ל תָּב֗וֹא וְשָׁ֤ם תָּמוּת֙ וְשָׁ֣ם תִּקָּבֵ֔ר אַתָּה֙ וְכָל־ אֹ֣הֲבֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁר־ נִבֵּ֥אתָ לָהֶ֖ם בַּשָּֽׁקֶר׃ס

passages.text: You have deceived me, O LORD, and I was deceived. You have overcome me and prevailed. I am a laughingstock all day long; everyone mocks me.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah speaks to the LORD.
Jeremiah says, “LORD, you deceived me.”
“I was deceived.”
“You overpowered me.”
“You prevailed against me.”
“I have become a laughingstock all day long.”
Everyone mocks me.
passages.original: פִּתִּיתַ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ וָֽאֶפָּ֔ת חֲזַקְתַּ֖נִי וַתּוּכָ֑ל הָיִ֤יתִי לִשְׂחוֹק֙ כָּל־ הַיּ֔וֹם כֻּלֹּ֖ה לֹעֵ֥ג לִֽי׃

passages.text: For whenever I speak, I cry out; I proclaim violence and destruction. For the word of the LORD has become to me a reproach and derision all day long.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is a prophet of the LORD.
Whenever I speak, I cry out.
I proclaim violence and destruction.
The word of the LORD has become a reproach to me.
People mock me all day long because of it.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ מִדֵּ֤י אֲדַבֵּר֙ אֶזְעָ֔ק חָמָ֥ס וָשֹׁ֖ד אֶקְרָ֑א כִּֽי־ הָיָ֨ה דְבַר־ יְהוָ֥ה לִ֛י לְחֶרְפָּ֥ה וּלְקֶ֖לֶס כָּל־ הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: If I say, “I will not mention Him or speak any more in His name,” His message becomes a fire burning in my heart, shut up in my bones, and I become weary of holding it in, and I cannot prevail.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is a prophet of the LORD.
Jeremiah sometimes wants to stop speaking about God.
Jeremiah says, “I will not remember God.”
Jeremiah says, “I will not speak again in God’s name.”
But God’s message burns inside Jeremiah’s heart like a fire.
This fire is shut up in Jeremiah’s bones.
Jeremiah tries to hold it in.
Jeremiah becomes tired from holding it in.
Jeremiah cannot keep it inside.
passages.original: וְאָמַרְתִּ֣י לֹֽא־ אֶזְכְּרֶ֗נּוּ וְלֹֽא־ אֲדַבֵּ֥ר עוֹד֙ בִּשְׁמ֔וֹ וְהָיָ֤ה בְלִבִּי֙ כְּאֵ֣שׁ בֹּעֶ֔רֶת עָצֻ֖ר בְּעַצְמֹתָ֑י וְנִלְאֵ֥יתִי כַּֽלְכֵ֖ל וְלֹ֥א אוּכָֽל׃

passages.text: For I have heard the whispering of many: “Terror is on every side! Report him; let us report him!” All my trusted friends watch for my fall: “Perhaps he will be deceived so that we may prevail against him and take our vengeance upon him.”
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is a prophet of the LORD.
Many people whisper about Jeremiah.
They say, “Terror is on every side!”
They say, “Report him! Let us report him!”
All of Jeremiah’s trusted friends watch for his downfall.
They say, “Perhaps he will be deceived.”
They say, “Then we can prevail against him.”
They say, “Let us take our vengeance upon him.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֜עְתִּי דִּבַּ֣ת רַבִּים֮ מָג֣וֹר מִסָּבִיב֒ הַגִּ֙ידוּ֙ וְנַגִּידֶ֔נּוּ כֹּ֚ל אֱנ֣וֹשׁ שְׁלוֹמִ֔י שֹׁמְרֵ֖י צַלְעִ֑י אוּלַ֤י יְפֻתֶּה֙ וְנ֣וּכְלָה ל֔וֹ וְנִקְחָ֥ה נִקְמָתֵ֖נוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: But the LORD is with me like a fearsome warrior. Therefore, my persecutors will stumble and will not prevail. Since they have not succeeded, they will be utterly put to shame, with an everlasting disgrace that will never be forgotten.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is with me.
The LORD is like a mighty and fearsome warrior.
My persecutors will stumble.
My persecutors will not prevail.
They have not succeeded.
They will be put to great shame.
Their disgrace will last forever.
No one will ever forget their everlasting shame.
passages.original: וַֽיהוָ֤ה אוֹתִי֙ כְּגִבּ֣וֹר עָרִ֔יץ עַל־ כֵּ֛ן רֹדְפַ֥י יִכָּשְׁל֖וּ וְלֹ֣א יֻכָ֑לוּ בֹּ֤שׁוּ מְאֹד֙ כִּֽי־ לֹ֣א הִשְׂכִּ֔ילוּ כְּלִמַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם לֹ֥א תִשָּׁכֵֽחַ׃

passages.text: O LORD of Hosts, who examines the righteous, who sees the heart and mind, let me see Your vengeance upon them, for to You I have committed my cause.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts examines the righteous.
The LORD sees the heart and mind.
I ask the LORD to let me see His vengeance upon my enemies.
I have committed my cause to the LORD.
passages.original: וַיהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ בֹּחֵ֣ן צַדִּ֔יק רֹאֶ֥ה כְלָי֖וֹת וָלֵ֑ב אֶרְאֶ֤ה נִקְמָֽתְךָ֙ מֵהֶ֔ם כִּ֥י אֵלֶ֖יךָ גִּלִּ֥יתִי אֶת־ רִיבִֽי׃ס

passages.text: Sing to the LORD! Praise the LORD! For He rescues the life of the needy from the hands of evildoers.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD saves people who are in need.
The LORD rescues the needy from evil people.
Sing to the LORD.
Praise the LORD.
passages.original: שִׁ֚ירוּ לַֽיהוָ֔ה הַֽלְל֖וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֥י הִצִּ֛יל אֶת־ נֶ֥פֶשׁ אֶבְי֖וֹן מִיַּ֥ד מְרֵעִֽים׃ס

passages.text: Cursed be the day I was born! May the day my mother bore me never be blessed.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is speaking.
Jeremiah is a prophet.
Jeremiah feels deep sorrow.
Jeremiah says, "Cursed be the day I was born."
He says, "May the day my mother gave birth to me never be blessed."
passages.original: אָר֣וּר הַיּ֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻלַּ֖דְתִּי בּ֑וֹ י֛וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ יְלָדַ֥תְנִי אִמִּ֖י אַל־ יְהִ֥י בָרֽוּךְ׃

passages.text: Cursed be the man who brought my father the news, saying, “A son is born to you,” bringing him great joy.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is a prophet of the LORD.
Jeremiah speaks with deep sorrow.
Jeremiah says, “Cursed be the man who brought news to my father.”
This man told Jeremiah’s father, “A son is born to you.”
This news brought Jeremiah’s father great joy.
passages.original: אָר֣וּר הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֨ר בִּשַּׂ֤ר אֶת־ אָבִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יֻֽלַּד־ לְךָ֖ בֵּ֣ן זָכָ֑ר שַׂמֵּ֖חַ שִׂמֳּחָֽהוּ׃

passages.text: May that man be like the cities that the LORD overthrew without compassion. May he hear an outcry in the morning and a battle cry at noon, because he did not kill me in the womb so that my mother might have been my grave, and her womb forever enlarged.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is speaking.
Jeremiah is a prophet.
Jeremiah feels deep sorrow and despair.
Jeremiah refers to a man who brought news of his birth.
May that man become like the cities the LORD destroyed without pity.
May that man hear cries of distress in the morning.
May that man hear the sound of battle at noon.
This is because that man did not kill me in the womb.
If he had, my mother would have been my grave.
Her womb would have remained enlarged forever.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַה֔וּא כֶּֽעָרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־ הָפַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א נִחָ֑ם וְשָׁמַ֤ע זְעָקָה֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וּתְרוּעָ֖ה בְּעֵ֥ת צָהֳרָֽיִם׃ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ מוֹתְתַ֖נִי מֵרָ֑חֶם וַתְּהִי־ לִ֤י אִמִּי֙ קִבְרִ֔י וְרַחְמָ֖הֿ הֲרַ֥ת עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: Why did I come out of the womb to see only trouble and sorrow, and to end my days in shame?
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is speaking.
Jeremiah is a prophet.
Jeremiah asks a question.
He says, “Why did I come out of the womb?”
He says, “I see only trouble.”
He says, “I see only sorrow.”
He says, “My days end in shame.”
passages.original: לָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ מֵרֶ֣חֶם יָצָ֔אתִי לִרְא֥וֹת עָמָ֖ל וְיָג֑וֹן וַיִּכְל֥וּ בְּבֹ֖שֶׁת יָמָֽי׃פ
